name: TERRACOTTA HORSE OF BANKURA
craft_technique: Hollow wheel-thrown components assembled by hand with incised clay applique
traditional_use: Votive offering placed under sacred Banyan groves for Dharmathakur and local protective village deities to invoke blessings and fulfillment of vows.
cultural_significance: Globally recognized emblem of Indian rural folk aesthetic; characterized by monumental erect ears, extended neck, and symmetrical architectural dignity.
associated_practice: Gram-devata worship ceremonies and annual Rarh region harvest melas.

dimensions.validation_notes: Measured from base of hoofs to tip of erect ears.

texture.value: Porous earthenware with impressed clay pellet jewelry

shape.value: Stylized tall quadruped with tubular neck and leaf-shaped ears

condition.value: Good; minor clay flake near left ear apex

craft_technique.value: Four wheel-thrown hollow legs joined to hollow body

condition_notes.cracks: Hairline firing fissure along underside belly, sealed naturally during kiln bake.
condition_notes.breakage: Tiny 1mm chip on tip of left ear.
condition_notes.discoloration: Kiln flash smoking marks on flank.

oral_knowledge.speaker: Sudhir Kumbhakar
oral_knowledge.status: Community-provided audio / Awaiting Institutional archive review
oral_knowledge.transcript: আমাদের পাঁচমুড়ায় বংশপরম্পরায় মাটির ঘোড়া গড়া হয়। চাকার ওপর আগে চারটে পা, ঘাড় আর শরীর আলাদা তৈরি করে তারপর হাতে জুড়ে নকশা বসাই। এটি ধর্মঠাকুরের থানে মানতের ঘোড়া।
oral_knowledge.translation: In our Panchmura village, terracotta horses have been created across generations. Four legs, the towering neck, and body are thrown separately on the potter's wheel, then joined together and decorated with clay pellets. It is dedicated as a vow at Dharmathakur village shrines.

cultural_origin.name: Panchmura, Bankura District, West Bengal
cultural_origin.details: Folk pottery hamlet of traditional Bankura terracotta artists.

community_region.name: Bishnupur Terracotta Belt
community_region.details: Famous heritage region known for Malla-era terracotta temples.

current_display.name: Bengal Craft Museum, Salt Lake, Kolkata

provenance.action: Sculpted and kiln-fired using local pit kiln.
